Claude Code Remote Control: continue sessions from your phone with an always-on Mac mini

Reviewed: 2026-11-20 · WodeMac

Remote Control is an official Claude Code feature. Start it with claude remote-control, or type /remote-control (or /rc) inside a session, then open the same session at claude.ai/code or in the Claude app for iOS and Android. Code execution and file access stay on the original machine. It is available on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise plans, not with API keys. Server mode (claude remote-control) runs several sessions from one process, so one machine can act as an always-available Claude Code host. The host has to stay on and the claude process has to keep running: a sleeping laptop pauses the work, and server mode exits after about 10 minutes without network. That is why many people run it on a Mac mini that never sleeps.

What it is

Remote Control turns the web and mobile apps into a window onto a session running on your own machine. Your filesystem, MCP servers, tools and project configuration stay available; messages from terminal, browser and phone stay in sync; you can attach photos and files from your phone. Unlike cloud sessions, nothing runs on Anthropic's infrastructure. The official docs say the computer has to stay on and the claude process has to keep running; closing the terminal or quitting the Desktop app takes the session offline.

On the network side, your local Claude Code makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports. Messages are routed through the Anthropic API over TLS, and the session transcript is stored on Anthropic servers while connected.

How to start it

Server mode shows a URL and, with the spacebar, a QR code for your phone:

claude remote-control

Interactive mode keeps the terminal usable while the session is also reachable remotely:

claude --remote-control

Inside an existing session, optionally with a name:

/remote-control My project

The Claude Desktop app and the VS Code extension use the same /remote-control or /rc command. Short forms work too: claude rc and claude --rc. Then open claude.ai/code or the Code tab in the Claude app and pick the session by name.

Server mode vs interactive mode

Server mode (claude remote-control) is a long-running process that does not need an open interactive session. It hosts several remote sessions at once, up to 32 by default (change it with --capacity). New sessions start in the current directory, or each in its own git worktree with --spawn worktree, so parallel tasks do not overwrite each other:

claude remote-control --name "My project" --spawn worktree

Interactive mode (claude --remote-control) and /remote-control inside a session handle one session per process; /remote-control carries over the current conversation.

They react differently to network loss. An interactive session keeps retrying and reconnects when the network returns. Server mode gives up after roughly 10 minutes and exits. After the server stops you can pick the work back up for about four hours with claude remote-control --continue or --session-id. The first run in a directory asks whether to trust it; without a terminal it exits with "Workspace not trusted", so confirm it once by hand.

Plans and sign-in

  • Available on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise subscriptions; API keys are not supported.
  • On Team and Enterprise an Owner must enable Remote Control in the Claude Code admin settings.
  • Sign in first with claude and /login; without an eligible login, claude remote-control exits with an error.
  • Not supported: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, tokens from claude setup-token, Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, or a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (gateways and proxies).

Details follow the official Claude Code documentation and may change.

Why an always-on Mac

Remote Control solves "I am away from my desk", not "my laptop went to sleep". Put the session on a machine that is always online and both problems disappear: run claude remote-control in the project directory (inside tmux if you like) and pick it up from anywhere. A WodeMac dedicated M6 Mac mini stays online 24/7 in California with Claude Code preinstalled; sign in with your own Claude subscription. Usage limits, tool updates and task errors still stop an agent, so keep branches, logs and stop conditions.

FAQ

Which plans include Remote Control?

Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise, according to the official docs. API keys are not supported, and Team or Enterprise owners must enable it first.

Does the code run on my phone?

No. Execution and file access stay on the machine where Remote Control was started; the phone and browser are only the interface.

What happens when the host laptop sleeps?

The session disconnects and the task stops. An interactive session reconnects when the machine is back online; server mode exits after about 10 minutes without network, and you resume with claude remote-control --continue. To keep tasks running, host the session on an always-on machine such as a dedicated Mac mini.

What is Remote Control server mode?

It is the claude remote-control command: one long-running process that hosts several remote sessions at once (32 by default), optionally each in its own git worktree with --spawn worktree. /remote-control inside a session and claude --remote-control handle one session per process.
